messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather data for the coordinates 40.7128 latitude and -74.0060 longitude?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

The user wants weather data for given coordinates. We need to use the tool `requests_get`. Likely we can call some API like open-meteo.com or other free service. But no specific endpoint was mentioned; maybe they expect us to fetch from openweathermap.org or similar.

We have to decide on a public API that doesn't require auth. For example, open-meteo.com provides current weather via:

https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...

But the tool expects certain params structure: url, optional headers, timeout, params dict containing lat/lon/format. So we could set url to something like "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". Then pass params {lat: 40.7128, lon:-74.0060}. Format param might be json. Also include additional required fields such as hourly temperature? Let's check open-meteo docs quickly mentally: They accept parameter "current_weather=true".

So our request would be: GET https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=40.7128&longitude=-74.0060&current_weather=true

Thus we need to supply those params accordingly. In the tool signature, params only includes lat,lon,format. There's no field for extra query strings. Hmm. That means this tool may not support arbitrary query parameters beyond lat, lon, format. That's limiting. Maybe there's another API that uses just lat/lon/format. Could be Nominatim geocoding? No.

Alternatively, perhaps we can use metaweather API: https://www.metaweather.com/api/location/search/?lattlong=40.7128,-74.0060 . But again requires custom query.

Given constraints, maybe we can't do it exactly. However, we can still attempt using open-meteo with minimal params: lat, lon, format=json. We'll get JSON output including forecast details. Might work because open-meteo accepts unknown params too. Even though tool restricts params keys, we can add them anyway? The schema says params has optional keys lat, lon, format. Additional keys likely ignored. But we cannot specify others. So we can't ask for current_weather flag. Without it, open-meteo returns default daily forecasts? Actually open-meteo defaults to returning many variables. Possibly fine.
